extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, naturalists, engineers and technical practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for assessing scientific books, technical notes, and brief technical/experimental reports (book reviews, letters, and technical descriptions) as exemplified in a Nature issue. Covers editorial submission policy, qualities of titles/illustrations/maps, treatment of subject-matter, clarity, and experimental apparatus/performance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor does not hold himself responsible for opinions expressed by his correspondents. Neither can he undertake to return, or to correspond with, the writers of, rejected manuscripts intended for this or any other part of Nature. No notice is taken of anonymous communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implications for contributors: do not send anonymous communications; do not expect correspondence or return of rejected manuscripts; opinions published by correspondents are their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a suitable and expressive title
rubrics_metrics.description: CHOOSING a suitable and expressive title is not unfrequently one of the most difficult tasks {next to writing a preface} in preparing a work relating to natural history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A title should be both suitable and expressive; avoid short/misleading covers that give an impression of different scope. The reviewer notes that a poor/ambiguous title can mislead reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title must reflect book content (avoid misleading short title)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title, 'European Animals,' which alone appears on the cover, suggests a work of a nature totally different from the one before us. At any rate, such was the impression in our own case, and we expected to find something in the shape of a text-book of at least the mammalian section of the European fauna. When the full title is read the situation is of course changed, although even then there seems something lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the cover/title accurately indicates scope and nature of the book; include sufficient qualifying/subtitle information to prevent false expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthiness and accuracy of maps
rubrics_metrics.description: A special feature is formed by a series of maps of the geographical distribution ... Assuming these maps to be trustworthy (and such of them as we have examined appear to be so), they have a very considerable value, for few things are more difficult than to obtain accurate information in such matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps are highly valuable only if reliable; reviewers will check sampled maps for accuracy. Inclusion of trustworthy distribution maps increases the scientific value of a work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and realism of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to most of the other illustrations, we regret, however, that we are unable to congratulate the author. They start with the disadvantage that they are taken from stuffed specimens — a style of illustration which does not appeal to our taste. Added to this is the circumstance that they have been largely 'faked' by the addition of false backgrounds. The least unsatisfactory is the frontispiece ... but even this is blurred and indistinct; ... Worst of all is the portrait ... of an apparently enraged hippopotamus careering on a mountain-top!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer photographic reproductions of natural (live or well-photographed) material (e.g., shells) over images of stuffed specimens or 'faked' backgrounds. Ensure clarity and appropriate background/context for illustrations; avoid exaggerated or misleading depictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of representative taxonomic groups for coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Having expressed his belief in the supreme value of mammals and land-snails to the student of distribution, the author, as might be expected, takes these groups as his text, using other sections of the animal kingdom as collateral evidence whenever occasion may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select groups that best serve the book's purpose (e.g., mammals and land-snails for zoogeography); explicitly justify taxon choice and use other groups as corroborative evidence rather than primary basis if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution and value to the field (inclusion in specialist libraries)
rubrics_metrics.description: The lectures ... contain so much valuable information that their publication was practically a duty owed by their author to the scientific world. The volume should be in the library of every naturalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a book contains sufficient new or consolidated information to merit recommendation for professional libraries; endorsement by established authorities (as cited) strengthens the recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid judging colonial/foreign conditions by old-world standards; present life-like, multi-faceted geography
rubrics_metrics.description: It is too much the custom for writers to judge the measures of a new country by old-world standards, and to commend or condemn them according to the degree of their correspondence. The volume is a compendium of geography; but the geography of to-day is a much wider subject than the dry-bone catalogues which formerly stood for that science... Under the heading of Physical, Economic, and Political Geography, the author has succeeded in presenting a life-like picture of the countries he describes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing about other regions, evaluate policies and conditions in their local context rather than by transplanting metropolitan norms. Cover physical, economic, and political geography to give a rounded, 'life-like' picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and simplification to produce valuable generalisations (ventilation literature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers on the subject of ventilation are apt either to deal with individual schemes ... or, armed with mathematics, to plunge ... which entirely obscures the main issue. It is the more satisfactory, therefore, to find a book free from such shortcomings. ... the author ... brings us, by a wise process of selection and rejection, to issues which, while admittedly approximate to truth, are at the same time most valuable generalisations, and this with a mathematical restraint which should considerably increase the field in which the utility of his work will be felt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applied-science texts, prefer clear selection of essential issues and restrained mathematical treatment that yields usable generalisations over exhaustive, inaccessible mathematical formalism or over-narrow case descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility of analogy and theoretical frameworks when tied to experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: The leading feature of the book is the development of the subject by the utilisation of an analogy between pneumatic and electrical flow and resistance ... The analogy is not confined to mere theorising. Actual apparatus ... is figured and described by which the fundamental pneumatic laws may be demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analogies (e.g., pneumatic-electrical) to clarify complex phenomena but support them with experimental demonstration and practical apparatus descriptions; present governing relations (e.g., H = R V*) and show real-world applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and conciseness of exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The diction throughout the book is so clear and concise that we cannot even quarrel with Dr. Shaw when he refers to a draught along the floor as likely to set up 'the reversed correlative of the therapeutic action' of putting one's feet in water, and we heartily endorse his suggestion that this important subject should receive more attention ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clear, concise writing that makes technical points accessible without sacrificing precision; maintain readable style even when discussing detailed theory or apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific thoroughness, currency of references, and organisation (brewing treatise)
rubrics_metrics.description: The present edition, like the previous ones, is essentially a treatise on the scientific principles which underlie brewing technology ... none of the more recent investigations of importance which bear on the subjects discussed appears to have been overlooked, and the references which are given add much to the value of the book. In one respect the late author and his colleague have lost an opportunity in not revising the original plan of the book, together with the matter it contains, for we have always considered that the book suffered to some extent in usefulness from the manner in which it was arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep editions updated with recent investigations and references; pay attention to organisation/plan of the book as arrangement can affect usefulness even when content is comprehensive. Identify strongest topic areas (e.g., chemistry of carbohydrates) and ensure they are well developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target readership recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend the book not only to those directly interested in the scientific aspect of brewing, but also to those chemists and biologists whose work in any way trends in the direction of brewing or malting problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and state which professional audiences should consult the work (practitioners, related-discipline scientists, librarians).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephotography — requirement: synchronous scanning and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The transmitting and receiving cylinders are caused to rotate synchronously, at the same time moving from end to end of their traverses; in the course of its spiral path the pinhole H covers successively every point of the focussed image ... The close spiral line with breaks in its uniformity constitutes a picture, which should be a counterpart of that projected upon T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure precise synchronous motion and traversal of transmitter and receiver so that each scanned element corresponds; mechanical synchronisation is critical for faithful reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephotography — selenium cell sensitivity and balancing (dynamic response compensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the transmitter a selenium cell S is used; to transmit a picture ... the resistance W is adjusted so that no current passes ... If now the Se cell darkened, its resistance will be increased and a current will pass ... Prof. Korn has succeeded in eliminating the effects of the sluggish component by substituting ... a second Se cell Sj, which ... by means of a second light-relay H2, placed in series with the first, is subjected to similar changes of illumination. Thus any subpermanent fall in the resistance of S1 due to the action of light is compensated by an equal fall in that of S2, and only such changes as respond immediately ... are utilised ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for detector temporal response (sluggishness) by using matched compensating detectors and relay circuitry so that only rapid (instantaneous) variations regulate the transmission current; employ balancing resistances and light-relays to stabilise baseline and improve fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephotography — modulation method (light-relay) and photographic receiver
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving cylinder R is covered with a sensitised photographic film or paper, upon a point of which light from a lamp is concentrated. Before reaching the paper the light passes through perforations in two iron plates ... between these is a shutter of aluminium leaf ... When a current traverses the wires, they are depressed by electromagnetic action, carrying the shutter with them, and a quantity of light proportional to the strength of the current is admitted through the perforations. By means of this 'light-relay' the intensity of the light acting at any moment upon the sensitised paper is made proportional to the illumination of the selenium in the transmitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a light-relay (electromagnetically-controlled shutter) to convert electrical modulation into proportional photographic exposure; calibrate lamp intensity, shutter aperture and timing to match transmitter dynamics and sensitised receiving medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephotography — reproduction of half-tones and gray-scale fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: His (Korn's) latest method ... a device of admirable ingenuity which has rendered it possible to transmit half-tones with fidelity. ... only such changes as respond immediately to the varying illumination of S1 are utilised for regulating the transmission current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reproduce half-tones, address detector non-linearity and temporal lag; use matched compensating detectors and appropriate modulation/demodulation so that gradations (gray levels) are preserved rather than only black/white edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wireless transmission — wavelength selection to mitigate daylight absorption
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that the daylight absorption was largely reduced between two stations 150 miles apart in Brazil by the use of a longer wave-length suggested ... With the longer frequency, though at night signals were considerably weaker ... the daylight signals were many times stronger, and it was found possible to work in daylight between Massachusetts and Cuba ... when using the lower frequency without any increase in sending power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For long-distance wireless links subject to daylight absorption, consider increasing wavelength (lower frequency) to reduce daytime absorption; be aware of trade-offs (night-time relative weakness, receiver tuning). Adapt wavelength with distance to overcome absorption phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wireless transmission — consider temporal and directional variability for meteorological inference
rubrics_metrics.description: The absorption comes on very suddenly ... The writer has found that the absorption at night-time varies with the direction from which the waves are received, and has obtained some results which seem to indicate that measurements of this phenomenon may have a meteorological value, and may assist in extending the range of weather forecasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and analyse temporal and azimuthal variations in signal absorption; such variability may be useful both for designing robust communication schedules and for extracting meteorological information.
